title: Featurizing Full Medical History for Modelling
section: Describe Basic Feature of Medical History
text:
Describe Basic Feature of Medical History
Now we can add features derived from each patients medical history. Here the “history” is every time they were assigned a unique ICD code on a specific date, so a 2-column tibble with the columns encounter_date and ICD_code. From such a table we can compute the following features and what they may represent to our models

How we featurize each patient’s medical history







Feature Name
Definition
Interpretation




n_codes
total codes assigned (unique date + code)



n_unique_codes
unique codes assigned
how many conditions does the patient have? health “prior”?


history_length
time between first and most recent visit
extensive medical history? many conditions? access to healthcare?


n_visits
number of unique visits recorded
same as length, but maybe better


most_common_code
which code was assigned the most frequently to the patient
their longest known condition? (appears on multiple visits)


most_common_code.freq
how frequently the most common code was assigned out of all codes assigned
how long they’ve known about theyre longest known condition (# of visits


code_frequency
n_codes / history_length

title: BSR 1715 Final Project
text:
For this project we examine the Mt. Sinai Millions Cohort, investigating patients experiences with Suicidal Ideation and/or Actions. Here are the steps in our analysis for clean + investigating + interpreting the data:

Patient Demographics & Outcomes
Featurizing Medical History Per Patient
Linear Modelling
Bootstrapping

title: Patient Demographics and Outcomes
text: The dataset is for patients part of the Mt. Sinai Millions (MSM) cohort, for each patient we have some demographic information and their “medical history”. The medical history is the list of ICD codes (specifiyng diagnoses) assigned to a patient by a doctor during a hospital visit for all recorded vists for that patient. So for every visit recorded we have the set of ICD codes assigned. We will turn this long-form medical history into a set of descriptive features for each patient that are better suited to linear modelling where patients are independent data points. We also use the medical history to define the outcome we are studying for each patient and whether they experience SI, Broad SA or Narrow SA.

Plot individual distributions for all 40280 patients with no missing data.


Code
make_single_ggbar <- function(col_name, plot_df=demographics_df){
    plot_df %>% 
    select(!!sym(col_name)) %>%
    count(!!sym(col_name)) %>% 
    add_column(feature=col_name) %>%  # dummy x-axis
    mutate(pct=prop.table(n)) %>%  # counts to percentages
    arrange(!!sym(col_name)) %>% 
    mutate(ypos=1 - (cumsum(pct) - pct/2)) %>%  # percentage label position on figure
    {
        ggplot(
            data=.,
            aes(
                x=feature,
                y=pct,
                fill=.data[[col_name]],
            )
        ) + 
        geom_col(position='stack') +  # stacked bar plot
        geom_text(
            aes(
                label=scales::percent(pct, accuracy=0.1),
                y=ypos
            ),
            vjust=0.5,    # nudge above top of bar
            size = 3
        ) + 
        scale_y_continuous(labels=scales::percent) +
        guides(fill=guide_legend(ncol=1)) +
        make_ggtheme() +
        theme(
            legend.position='right',
            axis.title=element_blank()
        )
    }
}

title: Patient Demographics and Outcomes
text:
Defining Patient Outcomes
For every patinent we want to create a discrete output column that specifies what experience (if any) the patient had with Suicidal Ideation or Actions. We have 3 lists of ICD codes, where for each list a patient is a “case” if they were assigned a matching code >= 1 time, and control otherwise. These “directly” observed outcomes are:

Ideation (SI)
Broad Action (Broad SA)
Narrow Action (Narrow SA)
Substance Use Disorder (Substance UD)
Alcohol Use Disorder (Alcohol UD)

We can further define outcomes based on combinations of SI, BSA and NSA. Each of these combinations excludes some set of samples to make the case/control comparison more clearly interpretable.

Now we can plot Case/Control frequencies for each outcome


Code
direct_outcomes <- unique(load_ICD_Phenotype_Mappings()$outcome.type)
# all_patient_outcomes_df
all_patient_outcomes_df %>% 
    select(FID, outcome.type, case_control_status) %>%
    mutate(outcome.definition=ifelse(outcome.type %in% direct_outcomes, 'direct', 'inferred')) %>% 
    group_by(
        outcome.definition,
        outcome.type,
        case_control_status
    ) %>% 
    summarize(n=n()) %>%
    mutate(pct=prop.table(n)) %>%  # counts to percentages
    mutate(ypos=1 - (cumsum(pct) - pct/2)) %>%  # percentage label position on figure
    {
        ggplot(
            data=.,
            mapping=
                aes(
                    x=outcome.type,
                    y=pct
                )
        ) + 
        geom_col(aes(fill=case_control_status), position='stack') +  # stacked bar plot
        geom_text(
            aes(
                label=scales::number(n, scale_cut=scales::cut_short_scale()),
                y=ypos
            ),
            vjust=0.5,    # nudge above top of bar
            size = 3
        ) + 
        facet_grid(
            cols=vars(outcome.definition),
            # rows=vars(metric),
            scales='free'
        ) +
        scale_y_continuous(labels=scales::percent) +
        make_ggtheme() +
        theme(
            axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=1, vjust=0.5),
            axis.title=element_blank(),
            legend.title=element_blank()
        )
    }
